current.text: Thompson is in Detroit's projected starting five, with Cunningham, Robinson, Collins and Duren.
Coach J.B. Bickerstaff says Thompson will play more than 26 minutes a game.
Experts do not trust Bickerstaff's minutes comments, because he has misled about Thompson's minutes and health before. They still expect about 2 to 4 more minutes a game than last season.
At about 26 minutes he may only match his draft price. At 28 to 30 minutes he should beat it easily, and at 30 minutes he would be very good.
The front office wants him on the ball more. Some of the usage Tobias Harris had is meant to go to him.
His jump shot was rebuilt. The team expects about three three-point attempts a game and more midrange shots from him.

Experts expect more usage, a scoring rise and about one more assist a game, for about 4 to 4.5 assists. One expert hopes for 6 rebounds, 2 steals and a block on 54% shooting, with no threes. Another does not expect him to improve much as a player and sees the gain coming from minutes.
He has just signed a new contract.
One expert still worries about how he fits next to Jalen Duren.
If the plan to put Thompson and Duren on the ball is failing by January, Detroit may trade for a secondary playmaker at the deadline.

Experts call him underpriced and the best Pistons target. Upside is top 50, best case about 28th, if he adds usage, assists, minutes and a little three-point shooting. The downside is that his free throws stay dreadful.

Experts disagree on draft spot. Early October previews would take him in the 50s or 60s in category leagues, while the newest mock (October 14) calls pick 60 early and a September mock called pick 72 too early.
In an auction mock he went for 17 USD. Josh could see him going for up to 20 USD.
Detroit is projected to win 50 to 51 games and finish third or fourth in the East.
Detroit plays 4, 3 and 4 games in our playoff weeks 19 to 21. The team has 15 back-to-backs, and no rest risk is expected.

durable.text: His fantasy value comes from defensive stats, mainly steals. He is a consistently good steals player, with the most deflections in his group, and his steals are a league outlier.
He adds good blocks and rebounds for a wing.
He is a very poor free throw shooter, and his FT% is a league outlier on the weak side. He makes almost no threes.
His two-point shooting is okay, so his FG% helps a little for his position.
He is an elite NBA defender.
He creates more of his own shots now, but his efficiency on those plays is well below league average.
He is worth more in category leagues than in points leagues.
Detroit is built on defense. The front office wants only enough offense, not an offensive superstar.

note: He went for 16 USD in our league last season, the same as his Yahoo value, while ESPN values him at only 4 USD. A mock auction had him at 17 USD with talk of up to 20 USD. Around 15 to 18 USD is fair for a punt FT% build that wants elite steals, solid blocks and rebounds, and no threes. Early in the season, check whether he plays 28 or more minutes despite Bickerstaff's track record, and whether his assists move toward 4 and he takes about 3 threes a game.
